name: @madewithremy/sandbox
description: Command-and-control server for Remy dev sandboxes

scripts.//typecheck: Two programs, and both must pass: the root Node one, and the browser-agent one that the root tsconfig excludes. `tsc -p` needs no --noEmit — tsconfig.browser.json sets it.

//@typescript/typescript6: The TypeScript 6 JS compiler API, used by devTunnel/interfaces/schema/* to parse an app's source and derive JSON schemas for method inputs. It is imported under this exact specifier rather than aliased over `typescript`, which is what the dev tunnel's old repo did: an alias puts two packages that both ship a `tsc` bin in the same tree, and `node_modules/.bin/tsc` then becomes whichever npm linked last. `typescript` here stays the TS7 native compiler that builds this package. A real dependency rather than a dev one, because the schema code imports it at RUNTIME — the old repo left it a devDependency and relied on the devbox image's global `typescript@6` (CLASSIC_TS_MAJOR) resolving by an upward walk from the global node_modules.
//browser-agent deps: `rrweb` and `@zumer/snapdom` are the browser agent's only external imports, and they are devDependencies ON PURPOSE: scripts/build-browser-agent.mjs inlines them into dist/browserAgent/index.js, so they are build-time inputs rather than runtime ones and the published package's dependency tree does not carry them. A box installs neither.
//rrweb pin: EXACT versions, no caret, and rrweb especially. The old browser-agent repo asked for `^2.0.0-alpha.4` and was held at alpha.4 only by its lockfile; installing that same range fresh here resolved rrweb 2.1.6, because a caret on a prerelease still admits the whole 2.x stable line. That would have swapped the recording engine underneath replay as a side effect of moving files. The event format is a cross-repo contract — the editor's rrweb player and youai-api's common/Recordings/stitch.ts both read these events — so an rrweb upgrade needs to be its own deliberate, tested change. Pinning makes the bundle reproducible and byte-comparable to what unpkg serves.

allowScripts.//esbuild: Two entries on purpose, and both are needed: 0.28.x is the direct dependency devTunnel/execution/transpiler.ts uses, 0.27.7 is what `tsx` pins, and npm matches these keys on exact version. esbuild's postinstall links its platform binary — without it the JS API throws at runtime, which in a box means every method transpile fails. The devbox image passes `--allow-scripts=...,esbuild,...` by name, so it is covered there regardless; these keys are what make a local install and CI agree with it.
